title: French Students Continue School Blockades as Tensions Rise
subtitle: Students demand better school conditions and lower living costs as the government warns that final exams are now in danger.

summary.en: High school students across France have resumed blocking school entrances after the autumn holiday. The protesters are calling for better building conditions, more teachers, and help with the rising cost of living. Government officials warn that the long-term absence from classes puts final exams at risk. Students’ unions argue that these protests are the only way to make the government listen to their concerns. A larger national strike is planned for later this week to support the students.
summary.zh: 法國各地高中生在秋假結束後恢復封鎖校門的抗議行動。抗議者要求改善校舍條件、增加教師人數，並針對日益高漲的生活成本提供協助。政府官員警告，長期缺課將使畢業考試面臨風險。學生工會則主張，這些抗議是讓政府傾聽他們訴求的唯一手段。本週稍晚將舉行全國性的大規模罷工，以聲援學生。

paragraphs.en: High school students in France returned to their protest movement this week, blocking school entrances in cities across the country. Following a two-week school holiday, students in Paris, Lille, Toulouse, and Marseille used wheelie bins to prevent access to school buildings. These actions are part of a protest movement that began in September, focusing on poor school conditions, a need for more teachers, and the high cost of living.
paragraphs.zh: 法國高中生本週重啟抗議行動，封鎖了全國多個城市的校門。在為期兩週的秋假結束後，巴黎、里爾、土魯斯和馬賽的學生利用大型垃圾桶阻擋校舍入口。這些行動是自九月開始的抗議運動的一部分，訴求重點在於改善校園環境、增加教師人力以及應對高昂的生活成本。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, students’ unions have ignored calls from President Emmanuel Macron to end the blockades. Nathanaël Combary, a member of the students’ union Renouveau Lycéen, stated that students must continue their "battle of strength" with the government. He argued that the measures offered by officials last week, such as plans to change class sizes and update university application systems, were not enough. Combary told BFMTV that while it is unfortunate that students must take such actions to be heard, they feel it is the only way to force a government response.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》報導，學生工會無視總統馬克宏（Emmanuel Macron）要求結束封鎖的呼籲。學生工會「高中生復興」（Renouveau Lycéen）成員納塔內爾·孔巴里（Nathanaël Combary）表示，學生必須繼續與政府進行這場「實力之爭」。他認為官員上週提出的措施，例如調整班級規模和更新大學申請系統的計畫，遠遠不足。孔巴里向法國商業調頻電視台（BFMTV）表示，雖然學生必須採取這種手段才能被聽見令人遺憾，但他們認為這是迫使政府回應的唯一途徑。

paragraphs.en: There is a significant disagreement regarding the scale of these protests. The French education ministry reported that 41 high schools were blocked on Monday, which represents about 1% of the total schools in the country. However, students’ unions claimed the number was much higher, estimating that 150 schools were affected. Meanwhile, police officers were seen outside several locations attempting to clear the barricades, which led to some arrests.
paragraphs.zh: 對於抗議規模，各方存在顯著分歧。法國教育部報告稱，週一有四十一所高中遭到封鎖，約佔全國學校總數的百分之一。然而，學生工會聲稱實際數字高得多，估計有一百五十所學校受到影響。與此同時，警方被目擊在多個地點試圖清除路障，這導致了一些逮捕行動。

paragraphs.en: Government officials have expressed deep concern about the impact on education. The education minister, Édouard Geffray, warned that the school year is now "at risk" for many students. He noted that hundreds of thousands of pupils in their final years have missed weeks of classes. Because of this, he said many students may not be able to finish their coursework or prepare properly for the baccalauréat, the important final exam taken at the end of high school. Geffray described the blockades as "illegal" and stated that his main goal is to get children back into their classrooms.
paragraphs.zh: 政府官員對教育受到的影響表示深切擔憂。教育部長愛德華·傑弗雷（Édouard Geffray）警告，許多學生的學年現在「岌岌可危」。他指出，數十萬名高年級學生已經錯過了數週的課程。因此，他表示許多學生可能無法完成課業，或無法為高中畢業會考（baccalauréat）做好充分準備，這是高中結束時的重要最終考試。傑弗雷形容這些封鎖行動是「違法」的，並表示他的首要目標是讓孩子們回到教室。

paragraphs.en: Teachers and school leaders have also shared their concerns. Nicolas Bonnet, from the headteachers’ union SNPDEN-UNSA, said it is time for everyone to return to their primary job of teaching and supporting pupils. He agreed that the current situation threatens final-year exams and university applications, though he acknowledged that students feel the government has not listened to their needs for a long time.
paragraphs.zh: 教師和學校領導階層也表達了他們的擔憂。來自校長工會「全國學校校長工會」（SNPDEN-UNSA）的尼古拉·邦內（Nicolas Bonnet）表示，現在是所有人回歸教學與輔導學生本職的時候了。他認同目前的局勢威脅到畢業考與大學申請，但也承認學生們確實感到政府長期以來忽視了他們的需求。

paragraphs.en: In some areas, the tension between protesters and authorities has led to conflict. In Montpellier, a video showed a 53-year-old school nurse being forced to the ground and handcuffed by police near a barricade. The local prefect, who oversees police operations, defended the arrest by saying the woman had resisted police and insulted officers. However, the Socialist senator Hussein Bourgi accused the government of "misconduct" and "provocation" regarding the incident.
paragraphs.zh: 在某些地區，抗議者與當局之間的緊張關係引發了衝突。在蒙佩利爾，一段影片顯示一名五十三歲的校護在路障附近被警方強行壓制在地並上銬。負責監督警務的當地省長為逮捕行動辯護，稱該女子拒捕並侮辱警員。然而，社會黨參議員胡笙·布爾吉（Hussein Bourgi）指責政府在該事件中存在「不當行為」與「挑釁」。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the situation is expected to become more complex. University students are planning to set up their own barricades at faculties, and trade unions have called for a large-scale strike on Thursday. This planned strike aims to bring together rail workers, teachers, and private-sector employees to support the students' demands. As the government and the protesters remain in a standoff, the future of the school year remains uncertain for thousands of young people across France.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，局勢預計將變得更加複雜。大學生計畫在各學院設置自己的路障，工會也已號召在週四進行大規模罷工。這場計畫中的罷工旨在集結鐵路工人、教師和私部門員工，以支持學生的訴求。隨著政府與抗議者持續僵持，法國成千上萬名年輕人的學年未來仍充滿不確定性。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop someone or something from moving through or into a place.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（積木），這裡作動詞用，指阻擋出入口。文中：High school students in France returned to their protest movement this week, blocking school entrances in cities across the country.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To remove people or things from a place to make it empty.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作形容詞（清楚的），這裡作動詞用，指移除路障。文中：Meanwhile, police officers were seen outside several locations attempting to clear the barricades, which led to some arrests.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A situation in which an agreement cannot be reached because neither side will change their position.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞片語 stand off 演變而來的名詞，指雙方互不相讓的狀態。文中：As the government and the protesters remain in a standoff, the future of the school year remains uncertain for thousands of young people across France.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，學生在巴黎、里爾、土魯斯和馬賽等地使用「wheelie bins」（輪式垃圾桶）來阻擋學校入口。選項 A 錯誤，因為路障是學生設置的，警察是後來才到場移除路障。選項 C 與 D 皆未在文中提及作為阻擋工具，屬於無中生有的干擾選項。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why are students likely to continue their protest despite the government's offers?

options.A: They want to cancel the baccalauréat exam entirely.
options.B: They believe the government's proposals do not address their core concerns.
options.C: They are being forced to protest by their teachers and school leaders.
options.D: They want to ensure the school year is extended for everyone.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第二段，學生會成員 Nathanaël Combary 明確表示，政府提出的班級規模調整與大學申請系統更新等措施「不足夠」（not enough），且學生認為這是迫使政府回應的唯一方式，隱含了學生認為政府目前的讓步並未解決他們關於生活成本與教學條件的核心訴求。選項 A、C、D 皆與文中描述的學生動機不符。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'at risk' mean in the context of the school year?

options.A: In danger of failing or not being completed successfully.
options.B: Extremely profitable for the education ministry.
options.C: Highly likely to be shortened by the government.
options.D: Protected from any further student interference.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境下，「at risk」意指學年面臨無法順利完成、課程進度落後或學生無法準備期末考試的危險。教育部長擔心學生錯過課程會導致無法完成學業。選項 B 與原意相反；選項 C 雖然提到學年受到影響，但並非指政府主動縮短學年；選項 D 與文意完全相反，因為學年正處於被干擾的狀態。
